Hi all - thanks for the sample, Grace. I've drafted a short evaluation plan and wanted to call out the specifics so everyone is aligned. High-level: 

Evaluation approach (draft):
- Dataset: use the 200 prompt sample + 1k anonymized messages. Split 80/20 for dev vs. eval (we will stratify by message type where present).
- Metrics:
  - Accept rate (clinical reviewer accept) - binary label; target >= 0.85 for pass
  - Accuracy of suggested triage label (top-1) - target >= 0.80
  - Response latency: P50 < 300ms, P95 < 800ms
  - Safety/PII checks: zero unredacted PHI in outputs (we'll run an automated scanner and manual spot checks)
- Scoring: weighted score (accept rate 40%, triage accuracy 30%, latency 20%, safety 10%) - pass threshold 0.75
- Baseline: run Redwood's best-open-model baseline + small quantized candidate; compare with tuned variant if time permits.

Deliverables and timeline: 
- 6/12: receive logs + prompt CSV (Grace)
- 6/13-6/16: data ingest + baseline runs
- 6/17: first scoring report (dev set)
- 6/19: evaluation report + recommendations (final baseline)

Questions / ask for Grace & Tom:
1) Can you confirm whether messages include structured triage labels today (e.g., urgent/routine) so we can use them as weak labels?
2) Are there any special categories (e.g., behavioral health) we should exclude from automated scoring?

I'll upload the evaluation spreadsheet to the Drive folder this afternoon and include instructions for the anonymized JSONL format we need (one message per line with the following fields: id, message_text, created_at, clinician_label). If you prefer, we can accept CSV instead.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
